key_insight: Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ shows magnetoresistive memory where resistivity depends on both the size and history of the applied magnetic field, and this appears unusually in the paramagnetic phase above the antiferromagnetic transition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new materials platform for nonvolatile sensing or memory devices that can encode magnetic-field history without requiring long-range magnetic order.
method: Measured resistivity versus magnetic field, temperature, and field-history protocols.
Compared behavior across the antiferromagnetic transition and into the paramagnetic regime.
Analyzed time dependence to assess whether metastability or short-range correlations drive the effect.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the MRM onset occurs at about twice the antiferromagnetic transition temperature and shows strong field-, temperature-, and time-dependent resistivity changes.
watch_item: The mechanism is still unresolved, so hidden order or fluctuating short-range correlations would need direct confirmation before device implementation.
paper_title: Magnetoresistive Memory in the Paramagnetic Phase of Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$
